metadata.note: The New Orleans Great Northern (Ozone Route), operator 1906 - June 30, 1933, and its predecessor the East Louisiana Railroad (1893 - 1905 as drawn). One feature per drawable span and operator (Rule 4). Every NOGN span ending in 1933 ends at the July 1, 1933 lease to the Gulf, Mobile and Northern, not at a service end; the GM&N and GM&O continuations are drawn in gulf_mobile_and_northern_railroad.geojson and are not redrawn here. Geometry for the alignments the GM&N layer already traced is cut from that layer's coordinates (identical shapes).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 40.3 mi against a documented 44.6 mi (Nov 1909 Guide: New Orleans 0 - Florenville 44.6). Cut from gmn-jackson-ms-new-orleans; its caveats carry forward. New Orleans - Slidell (30.1 mi traced vs 34.7 documented) is TRACKAGE RIGHTS over ANOTHER COMPANY'S TRACK, the Southern's New Orleans and Northeastern, drawn on the present NS NO&NE District (old_railway_operator=Southern) across the Lake Pontchartrain trestle; it is drawn here only because NOGN trains ran over it. STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS: the final 2.8 mi from the NO&NE at Almonaster/Press St. to the site of New Orleans Terminal Station (Canal and Basin streets; approach tracks lifted) is a straight line, not the historical approach route; and a 0.34 mi straight join at Slidell where the Southern and GM&O-tagged traces meet. Slidell - North Slidell - Florenville (10.3 mi traced vs 9.9 documented) is on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O. LATER ALIGNMENT: corridor as mapped today; the 1909-1933 lake-trestle and city approach alignments were not separately verified. Terminal Station was the New Orleans terminal for all drawn years (from 1908; the Press St. terminal used 1906-1908 falls before this span).

segments.note: New Orleans (Terminal Station) - Slidell - North Slidell - Florenville. Start 1909 = the Nov 14, 1909 Official Guide, the first source showing the main line via North Slidell (trains 62/63 New Orleans - Jackson plus 54/55, 56, 58, 59 to Bogalusa / West Columbia). START BRACKET 1906-1909: NOGN trains reached Florenville from New Orleans by Dec 1906, but the route they took is NOT established - either the NO&NE to Slidell and NOGN's new Slidell - Florenville line, or the NO&NE to Pearl River and the ex-ELR (see nogn-pearl-river-branch) - so 1906-1908 are withheld here rather than guessed. New Orleans terminal: Press St. 1906-1908, Terminal Station from 1908. New Orleans - Slidell (34.7 mi) was trackage rights over the New Orleans and Northeastern (Southern / Queen and Crescent); NOGN's own rails began at Slidell (depot shared with the NO&NE, 1913 building). 1913 tt: Nos. 2, 4, 8, 10, 12 plus Sunday-only and Bogalusa trains. Sept 1922: NOGN warned it might 'have to discontinue some of its passenger trains' because of bus competition - a threat, not a discontinuance. END = the July 1, 1933 lease of the reorganized NOGN Railway to the Gulf, Mobile and Northern (Lemly ch. XXI), not a service end; the GM&N-era continuation is drawn in gulf_mobile_and_northern_railroad.geojson. SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: Lemly ch. VIII says that after Feb 1930 the NOGN 'ceased to exist as an operating entity. It became the Louisiana Division of the GM&N' - which would put the split at 1930; ch. XXI has the NOGN still a separate corporation and in its own receivership Nov 7, 1932 - June 1933. 1933 is used in both layers so they join without gap or overlap. Headway 360 is an estimate from the 1909 and 1913 tables (about four trains each way); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: Official Guide Nov 14, 1909 schedules (Sept 1910 Guide page); NOGN public timetable eff. Mar 30, 1913; St. Tammany Farmer Dec 29, 1906 p.4; Lemly ch. XXI; Fowler LA line 8 (research report block [1]).

segments.note: Covington - Ramsay - Red Bluff - Onville - Folsom: extension 'the East Louisiana had built or operated' (Lemly); opening year not found. BOTH ENDS [OPEN]. START: 1906 is the earliest CONFIRMED year (St. Tammany Farmer, Dec 29, 1906: the 'St. Tammany Special ... will go through to Folsom, as at present'), not a known start. END: 1913 is the last CONFIRMED year (NOGN tt Mar 30, 1913: all Shore Line trains Nos. 21-28 run to/from Folsom; Pfalzheim [Pruden] in a 1911 timetable per Fowler), NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger trains to Folsom stopped. The Sept 1922 NOGN statement that bus competition paralleled every foot 'with the exception of the line between Covington and Folsom, where there is practically no passenger business' suggests trains still ran but does not say so, and is not used to extend the span. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 480 is an estimate (1913: all Shore Line trains through to Folsom); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates (Rule 3).

All on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=GM&O (the ex-ELR grade, now Shinglemill Rd, Sid Crawford Rd, Dummy Line Rd and LA-36 / Hickory Highway), no straight-line legs. Starts at the junction with the Southern's NO&NE at Pearl River; crosses the NOGN main line at Florenville. St. Tammany end placed by projecting the GNIS point onto the grade (the point is 3.8 km off the grade; the projection falls at 9.5 mi, agreeing with Fowler's 9). Same geometry as the first 9.5 mi of elr-pearl-river-covington. LATER ALIGNMENT: road-converted grade as mapped today.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] - a single proven year. NOGN public timetable eff. Mar 30, 1913, 'Pearl River Branch': Pearl River - Hill's Switch - Florenville - St. Tammany, Nos. 42/43 daily except Sunday and 44-48 Sunday, EVERY train headed 'Mixed' (mixed trains carried passengers, so this counts). The surviving stub of the East Louisiana's 1887 main line, NOGN-operated from June 1905. Service certainly ran wider than 1913 both ways, but no other NOGN passenger year is confirmed: the Nov 1909 Guide page has no Pearl River table (absence, not evidence) and nothing later was found. Do not widen or delete this anchor. Headway 1440 is an estimate; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: NOGN tt Mar 30, 1913 'Pearl River Branch' (every train headed Mixed); Fowler LA lines 9, 88; hawkinsrails NOGN page (research report block [5]).

segments.note: Pearl River - River Junction - Florenville - St. Tammany (Generelly) - Mandeville Junction - Pontchatalawa - Abita Springs - Claiborne - Covington; ELR trains ran in from New Orleans over the NO&NE. [OPEN] START - 1893 is the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year (River Switch tagged in the 1893 Official Guide, Fowler), not the opening: Pearl River - Abita Springs was completed June 1887 and Covington reached May 16, 1888 (one source says 1887) - construction dates, not proof of passenger trains, so 1887-1892 are withheld. END = sale to the New Orleans Great Northern, June 1, 1905 - an operator change, not a service end. The ELR 'inaugurated' the New Orleans - 'Ozone Belt' trains. Headway 720 is an estimate; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: Fowler LA line 88 (River Switch and Chinchuba tagged z = 1893 Official Guide, confirming passenger service on the main line and the Mandeville branch in 1893); opening and sale dates from Wikipedia, msrailroads and the Tammany Family blog, read via search snippets only, not in full (research report block [9]).
